purpose: Increase possible markets, not risk, and measure opportunity count versus net portfolio returns.

rate_policy.note: Read-only stock history beyond the Basic two-year window supports paid-stock-tier access; official paid stocks plans allow unlimited calls. Keep a paced stock-only client and fall back on HTTP429. No plan changes, and futures/crypto defaults stay unchanged.

notes: All 65 candidate instruments use original 5m confirmed-retest / 2R rules. Original sessions, two entries per asset/day, stops, costs and capital/risk controls stay fixed. No frequency-study wider hours or repeated entries.

Training screening uses the unchanged pool_protocol.json thresholds, completed pre-May trades, higher-cost stress and three early time blocks. top5_65 retains the existing maximum-five / one-per-exposure-bucket rule. eligible65 enables every training-eligible asset to test more possible markets; it does not rank using later returns.

all29 and all65 enable their entire predefined universes regardless of training results. Trade allocation remains alphabetical at a shared minute open, with 1% entry risk, 2% aggregate open risk, two concurrent positions, one equity-index future, 3% daily loss budget and capital reservations unchanged.

Use fresh $50k accounts on May-November and the same observed MNQ market-date clock. Reuse the 29 unchanged candidate journals and prior same-date all17, selected29 and MCL benchmarks with explicit provenance. Only the 36 additional candidates and eight new portfolio simulations require new replay.

Names are predefined surviving instruments, not a historical index universe, random sample, or proof of asset independence. Stock/ETF shorts and settled cash/broker buying power remain unmodeled. Intraminute paths are hypothetical and margin proxies are static.

Publish all candidates, unavailable data, training eligibility, all portfolio cases and fixed-fill stress. No new risk increase, target optimization, entry filter, rule search or live orders. This is another retrospective experiment on already inspected dates; increasing the search space also increases selection bias.
